faq.title: Questions I'm often asked
faq.q1: How does a first project work?
faq.a1: We start with a free 30-minute call to understand your context and needs. If the project is aligned, I send you a proposal with scope, timeline and rate. We usually start within one to two weeks.
faq.q2: Do you work on a time-and-materials or fixed-price basis?
faq.a2: Both, depending on the project. Short scoping missions are often fixed-price. Longer engagements (automation, PM) are on a daily or monthly rate. We define the best format together.
faq.a3: It varies depending on the nature and volume of the mission. I'll share my rates during our first call. I prefer long-term relationships over one-shot projects.
faq.q4: Do you work with already structured teams?
faq.a4: Yes, and that's actually where I add the most value. I know how to integrate into an existing environment, work with your devs, designers and ops, without friction.

realisations.meta_desc: Concrete client cases: automation, AI, product ops. Problem → Solution → Impact.
realisations.title: Projects
realisations.subtitle: Real projects, measurable results.

c1.title: Client onboarding automation
c1.problem: The client onboarding process was entirely manual: 6 steps, 3 different tools, 4 hours of processing per file. Data entry errors and delays were degrading the client experience.
c1.solution: Design and deployment of a complete n8n workflow: automatic trigger upon contract signature, access creation, email sequence dispatch, Slack notification, CRM update.
c1.impact: −80% processing time (from 4h to 45min). Zero data entry errors. Customer satisfaction +18pts on NPS.

c2.title: Internal AI assistant for a logistics team
c2.problem: Field teams were losing 2h/day searching for information across scattered documents (procedures, rates, contacts). No centralized tool, no RAG in place.
c2.solution: Full project scoping: model selection (Claude Sonnet), document corpus definition, interface specs, development steering with the internal team, testing and deployment.
c2.impact: +40% operational efficiency on document queries. >80% adoption within 3 weeks.

c3.title: Product ops restructuring
c3.problem: The product roadmap was driven by gut feeling. No OKRs, no prioritization ritual, chaotic sprint planning. Declining velocity, team frustration.
c3.solution: Implementation of a complete PM framework: quarterly OKRs, automated RICE scoring in Notion, weekly rituals, velocity dashboard. Reporting automation via Make.
c3.impact: +30% sprint velocity in 2 months. Backlog reduced by 60%. Team aligned on priorities.

c4.title: AI lead qualification pipeline
c4.problem: The sales team spent 3h/day manually qualifying inbound leads: website analysis, sector, size, potential. Inaccurate qualification, loss of hot leads.
c4.solution: Complete automated pipeline: data scraping and enrichment, AI scoring via GPT-4, automatic assignment to the right salesperson, CRM record creation with generated summary.
c4.impact: +25% conversion rate. −3h/day for the sales team. Positive ROI in < 6 weeks.

univers.meta_desc: Beyond work: competitive padel, esport world champion, football and event organisation.
univers.title: My universe
univers.subtitle: What I do when I'm not building.

padel.title: Padel — competitive level
padel.desc1: I've been playing competitive padel since 2021. Ranked P250, I train three times a week and regularly participate in amateur and open circuits in the Paris region.
padel.desc2: Padel taught me that tactical thinking and real-time adaptation are often worth more than raw power. Lessons I apply directly to my work: reading the situation, adjusting strategy, staying calm under pressure.

esport.title: World Champion — CS:GO
esport.desc1: In 2019, my team won the FACEIT World Championship in CS:GO, one of the most competitive tournaments on the amateur world scene. Several months of qualifications, thousands of teams, a final under maximum pressure.
esport.desc2: Esport shaped me as much as my studies. Managing a high-level collective, analyzing complex meta-games, performing under pressure in a world final — these are skills directly transferable to the professional world. Mastering complex systems, competitive mindset, rapid decision-making: this is my real school.

univers.quote: Competition taught me one essential thing: the difference between good and great is rarely talent — it's discipline, preparation, and the ability to stay lucid when the stakes are high.

evenement.title: Event Organisation
evenement.desc1: I've been organising events for several years — parties, tournaments, gatherings. From logistics to communication and on-site team coordination, I've learned to manage uncertainty and deliver a memorable experience despite the unexpected.
evenement.desc2: Running a successful event is exactly like running a project: anticipate, delegate, pivot fast. A school of operational discipline I apply every day in my freelance work.

football.title: Football — regular practice
football.desc1: Football has been part of my life since childhood. I play recreationally but with the intensity and discipline of a competitor: reading the game, collective pressing, defensive organisation. A sport that builds character as much as fitness.
football.desc2: Football taught me the value of the collective. You can have the best individuals in the world — without cohesion and a shared strategy, you don't win. A conviction I bring to every team I work with.
